The acting user, Karen Watkins (user 39), is an admin; the policy gives admins write access to configuration tables, so every step is in scope.
The benchmark's joins (topic detail to category, criteria to group, service to topic, template and criteria) are expressed as references to the ids of the rows this task creates: category 13, topic detail 36, group 19, criteria 8, template 7, service 55; each is the only row the task creates in its table.
The request says investigation cases start with 'the same default description and internal categorization' from the template but gives no values or keys, so the template's change_request_values (a JSON column) is not tested.
'Service template should be labelled with template At the end' is read as the name 'Employee Relations Confidential Investigation template', as the benchmark also reads it.
Active flags on the new category, detail, group, criteria and template are not stated and not tested; the service's active flag is required because employees raise cases through it.
The request names no members for the new team, so no membership is required.
The listed tools only create rows, so the stays record the request's explicit statements that existing rows are not repurposed; they hold on the seed and fail only if an existing row is overwritten or an extra criteria is added. No seed service links any criteria or template, so 'approvals already configured for other services' is read as the approval criteria rows themselves.
The request's prohibition on adding the area to General, HR Operations or HR System Support is enforced by the topic detail's topic_category = 13 and the service's topic_detail = 36; visibility of investigation cases to generalist groups is enforced through the criteria's user_group = 19, since the seed holds no other per-service visibility setting.
